title: Ramsey theory
summary: Every $2$-colouring of the edges of a large complete graph contains a monochromatic $K_k$. The Ramsey number $R(k)$ is the threshold; $\sqrt2^{\,k} \le R(k) \le 4^k$, improved to $(4-\varepsilon)^k$ in 2023.
why: Complete disorder is impossible: this one principle spans graphs, arithmetic progressions and logic.

timeline.title: Ramsey's theorem
timeline.text: Proved as a lemma about decision procedures in logic.

timeline.title: Random graphs bound Ramsey numbers
timeline.text: A counting argument shows $R(k) > 2^{k/2}$, the start of the probabilistic method.

title: The probabilistic method
summary: To show an object exists, pick one at random and show the probability it works is positive. Linearity of expectation, alterations, the Lovász local lemma and concentration inequalities are the main tools.
key_statements: \Pr\big[\text{some } K_k \text{ monochromatic}\big] \le \binom nk 2^{1-\binom k2} < 1 \Rightarrow R(k) > n
why: Erdős's 1947 Ramsey lower bound started it; it now drives coding theory, randomized algorithms and much of extremal combinatorics.

timeline.title: Random graphs bound Ramsey numbers
timeline.text: A counting argument shows $R(k) > 2^{k/2}$, the start of the probabilistic method.

title: Extremal set theory
summary: How large can a family of subsets of $[n]$ be under a restriction? Sperner bounds antichains, Erdős–Ko–Rado bounds intersecting families of $k$-sets, and the sunflower lemma finds structured subfamilies.
why: These bounds are the combinatorial core of results in coding theory, complexity lower bounds and the union-closed sets conjecture.

timeline.title: Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem
timeline.text: Intersecting families of $k$-subsets of $[n]$, $n\ge2k$, have at most $\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ members.

title: Hypergraphs
summary: Edges with any number of vertices. Turán and Ramsey questions become much harder: the Turán density of the $3$-uniform $K_4^{(3)}$ is still unknown.
why: Hypergraph regularity and container methods power modern proofs of Szemerédi-type theorems.

title: Grids, tilings and board colourings
summary: Problems on chessboards and grids: tiling regions with dominoes or polyominoes, placing pieces, and colouring the board so a counting argument rules a configuration out.
key_statements: \text{a mutilated } 8\times8 \text{ board (two opposite corners removed) has no domino tiling}
why: The colouring trick is an invariant in disguise; domino tilings link to determinants and statistical physics.

title: Combinatorial geometry
summary: Finite point sets in the plane: how many unit distances, how many distinct distances, when points must contain a convex $k$-gon, how lines and points can be incident.
why: Erdős's distance problems pushed incidence geometry into polynomial methods; in May 2026 an AI model found a counterexample to his unit distance conjecture.

timeline.title: The distinct distances problem
timeline.text: $n$ points determine $\gg n/\log n$ distinct distances, via the polynomial method.

timeline.title: Unit distance conjecture disproved
timeline.text: Reported counterexample to Erdős's 1946 conjecture on the maximum number of unit distances; Tim Gowers praised the proof.

title: Infinite combinatorics and partition calculus
summary: Ramsey theory for infinite sets and cardinals. The arrow notation $\kappa \to (\lambda)^n_r$ asks whether every colouring of $n$-subsets of $\kappa$ with $r$ colours has a homogeneous set of size $\lambda$.
why: Several of these questions are independent of ZFC, so the answer depends on the axioms.
